title: Benchmarking Screening Methods: Classification Accuracy
text: BenchAcc() compute classification accuracy screening methods according known ground truth treats "Positive" positive class every supported label ("Negative", "Neutral", "") negative class. screening method found object, computes full set binary classification metrics, methods can ranked compared exactly cells. function accepts three kinds input: Seurat object whose meta.data contains one column per screening method; ScreenMethodResult, unwrapped scRNA_data slot; BenchAccConfig, runs every configured screening method first evaluates merged labels one pass.

title: Benchmarking Screening Methods: Classification Accuracy
text: example uses tiny object six cells, ground-truth column two simulated screening results. real analysis Scissor scPAS columns produced Screen() MergeResult(). element returned list one-row matrix whose row name screening method. numbers easier compare binding :
code: counts <- Matrix::Matrix(   matrix(     seq_len(24L),     nrow = 4L,     dimnames = list(paste0("Gene", 1:4), paste0("Cell", 1:6))   ),   sparse = TRUE )  sc <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)  sc$truth <- c(   "Positive",   "Negative",   "Positive",   "Other",   "Positive",   "Negative" ) sc$Scissor <- c(   "Positive",   "Negative",   "Positive",   "Other",   "Negative",   "Negative" ) sc$scPAS <- c(   "Positive",   "Positive",   "Negative",   "Other",   "Negative",   "Negative" )  metrics <- BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE)  round(do.call(rbind, metrics), 3) #>           TPR   FPR   TNR   FNR  F1 Accuracy Precision Recall #> Scissor 0.667 0.000 1.000 0.333 0.8    0.833       1.0  0.667 #> scPAS   0.333 0.333 0.667 0.667 0.4    0.500       0.5  0.333 metrics_dt <- data.table::rbindlist(   lapply(metrics, as.data.frame),   idcol = "method" )  metrics_dt[, .(method, TPR, FPR, F1, Accuracy, Precision, Recall)] #>     method       TPR       FPR    F1  Accuracy Precision    Recall #>     <char>     <num>     <num> <num>     <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1: Scissor 0.6666667 0.0000000   0.8 0.8333333       1.0 0.6666667 #> 2:   scPAS 0.3333333 0.3333333   0.4 0.5000000       0.5 0.3333333

title: Extending SigBridgeR: A Guide for Custom Extensions
text: addition code formatting interface requirements described , several tips developing new algorithm: CODE STYLE: tidyverse style recommended. PARAMETER: Instead passing raw arguments directly algorithm, construct dedicated parameter object perform validation preprocessing inside object’s builder. checks normalization front keeps algorithm clean prevents malformed inputs reaching screening logic. parameter object validated proceed run algorithm. PERFORMANCE: algorithm computationally expensive, prioritize optimizing code reaching parallelization. Parallelization can multiply resource usage complexity, often masks inefficiencies better implementation remove. Consider following strategies, roughly order: cheapr data.table matrixStats sparseMatrixStats qs2 matrixTests stats::cor -> [WGCNA](https://github.com/cran/WGCNA)::cor Rewrite hot path high-performance language C++, Rust, Julia; Consider hardware accelerators GPU TPU. FILE STORE: non-temporary, meaningful intermediate analysis files need written, organize {method_name}_res directory. RESULT REPORT: result returned algorithm assign specific label every cell. can delivered simple vector (favor lightweight, minimal development) data.frame (comprehensive easier extend reuse). Avoid returning phenotype-association score, bare score difficult apply directly concrete studies. score suitable research material ; contrary, requires results study corroborate .

what: 1.1.1 Find the Optimal Normalization Method for Seurat
title: Full Tutorial
text: simple scoring function selecting normalization method. Evaluates 3 dimensions preprocessing quality: Variance stabilization: Decoupling mean-variance relationship normalized expression (lower correlation = better). Biological signal retention: Preservation known marker genes within highly variable genes (higher retention = better). Dropout robustness: Removal technical dropout bias normalized values (lower correlation dropout rate = better). Exmaple: Supports simultaneously adding Seurat objects preprocessed multiple methods, ensuring equivalent standard workflow NormalizeData + ScaleData + FindVariableFeatures. Parameters subset_size: Size single-cell data subset (.e., number cells) evaludated. known_hvgs: list character. Known highly variable genes, provided reference baseline. n_hvgs: Maximum number highly variable genes consider. low_expressed_thresh: Percentage genes excluded consideration, ranked expression level. weight: Scoring weight sum 1.
code: obj <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts)  sct <- Seurat::SCTransform(obj) lognorm <- Seurat::NormalizeData(obj) |>   Seurat::ScaleData() |>   Seurat::FindVariableFeatures()  res <- ChooseNormalization(   sct = sct,   lognorm = lognorm,   # * More can be added here   subset_size = integer(),   known_hvgs = list(),   n_hvgs = 2000L,   low_expressed_thresh = 0.2,   weight = c(     variance_stability = 0.4,     marker_signal = 0.35,     dropout_robustness = 0.25   ) ) res$metrics |> format() res$recommendation

code: set.seed(123) ngenes <- 1000 nsamples <- 1000  gene_names <- paste0("GENE", seq_len(ngenes)) sample_names <- paste0("Sample", seq_len(nsamples))  counts <- matrix(   rnbinom(ngenes * nsamples, mu = 100, size = 10),   nrow = ngenes,   ncol = nsamples,   dimnames = list(gene_names, sample_names) ) gene_length <- sample(   500:5000,   ngenes,   replace = TRUE ) names(gene_length) <- gene_names tpm <- CountsToTPM(counts, gene_length) tpm[1:5, 1:5] ##        Sample1   Sample2   Sample3   Sample4   Sample5 ## GENE1 602.7856 1078.0287  687.1092  514.0647  647.0981 ## GENE2 224.4745  335.5068  437.5985  556.4223  384.2567 ## GENE3 760.3323  262.8887  411.2022  511.3512  255.3896 ## GENE4 537.6406 1100.3214 1685.6017 1223.9918 1116.6870 ## GENE5 609.4410  452.0651  437.2982  840.6543  329.2632

Domain adaptation method, one "Wasserstein", "MMD". Default "Wasserstein". model_save_dir: Character. Directory used store trained model. Default "DEGASv2_res". lambda1, lambda2, lambda3: Numeric. DEGASv2 package must installed (pak::pak("Exceret/DEGASv2"), handled automatically Screen). Defaults 96L 8L. n_output: Integer. Output dimension encoder. Default 32L. nlayers: Integer. Number encoder layers. Default 3L. n_pred: Integer. Number prediction heads. Default 2L. dropout: Numeric. Dropout rate regularization. Default 0.5. encoder_type: Character. Encoder architecture, one "MLP", "Transformer", "DenseNet". infer_mode: Character. Inference mode, "SC" (single-cell) "ST" (spatial transcriptomics). Training n_trials: Integer. Number repeated training trials. Default 5L. do_reject: Logical. Whether apply rejection criteria uncertain predictions. Default TRUE. tolerance: Numeric. Tolerance threshold rejection. Default 0.05. Usage: TiRank supports caching, preprocessed data trained model can reused. Note final prediction table read <save_path>/3_Analysis/spot_predict_score.csv, keep save_path aligned cache directory used: note: TiRank currently runs GPU (device = "cuda" used internally), CUDA-capable device required. rTiRank package must installed (pak::pak("Exceret/rTIRank"), handled automatically Screen), Python dependencies provisioned automatically reticulate::py_require(). returning structure: list containing: scRNA_data: Seurat object screening, TiRank_Reject, TiRank_Rank_Score TiRank ("Positive", "Neutral", "Negative") added meta.data, parameters stored scRNA_data@misc$TiRank. cell_cell_distance: computed cell-cell similarity/distance matrix.

text: PhenoMapR derives gene-level reference matched bulk expression phenotype, scores every single cell labels two tails score distribution. Parameters pass ... using PhenoMapR method: Phenotype handling phenotype_column: Character NULL. Outcome column name binary/continuous phenotypes. Default NULL (uses "phenotype_value"). survival_time, survival_event: Character. Column names survival phenotype data frame. Defaults "time" "status". binary_positive_reference: Character. level binary phenotype treated reference-positive direction, "second" "first". Default "second". reference_sign: Integer. Sign applied reference scores, use -1 mirror score axis. Default 1L. Bulk reference construction normalize: Logical. Whether normalize bulk expression. Default TRUE. platform: Character. Bulk platform, one "auto", "rnaseq", "microarray". Default "auto". probe_annotation: Probe--gene annotation table microarray data. Default NULL. hugo_species: Character. Species passed HGNChelper, "human" "mouse". Default c("human", "mouse"). Single-cell scoring assay, layer: Character. Seurat assay layer used scoring. Defaults "RNA" "data". z_score_cutoff: Numeric. Z-score cutoff limiting paired genes. Default 2L. score_mode: Character. Scoring mode, one "weighted_sum", "activity_adjusted". vars_to_regress: Character vector. Variables regressed scoring. Default c("S.Score", "G2M.Score", "nCount_RNA"). cancer_type: Character NULL. Optional cancer-type context. Default NULL. pseudobulk: Logical. Whether score pseudobulk profiles instead single cells. Default FALSE. group_by: Character NULL. Grouping variable used pseudobulk aggregation. Default NULL. sample_metadata: Data frame NULL. Sample-level metadata used pseudobulk = TRUE. Default NULL. Group definition percentile: Numeric. Tail percentile used define phenotype groups. Default 0.05. permutation_n: Integer NULL. Number permutations. Default NULL. permutation_seed: Integer NULL. Permutation seed, defaults seed. Usage: note: PhenoMapR labels upper tail score distribution "Adverse" lower tail "Favorable", mapped package-wide vocabulary "Positive" "Negative"; cells middle labelled "Neutral". Higher scores follow phenotype-valued--1 direction reference derived default orientation. binary phenotypes means binary_positive_reference = "second" regresses "1" level, survival traits Cox z-score positive hazard-increasing genes. Therefore, phenotype 1 denotes unfavourable direction, "Adverse" tail one labelled "Positive". phenotype encoded way round, adjust binary_positive_reference set reference_sign = -1. returning structure: list containing: scRNA_data: Seurat object screening, group labels stored PhenoMapR column ("Positive", "Negative", "Neutral" NA) per-cell scores PhenoMapR_* columns meta.data. parameters used recorded scRNA_data@misc$PhenoMapR. phenomap_scores: Per-cell scores returned PhenoMapR::PhenoMap(). reference: gene-level reference z-scores derived bulk data.

title: Find Optimal Parameters for My Screening
text: scAB two key parameters, alpha alpha_2: former determines overall selection proportion, latter determines selection proportion within scAB subset. Simply change values two parameters single values numeric sequences, scAB automatically iterate combinations find optimal pair alpha alpha_2. can see, many (alpha, alpha_2) pairs – requiring evaluation – runtime can become prohibitively long. cases, parallel computing can employed accelerate process. Output goes like using example data identifying optimal (alpha, alpha_2) pair, scAB use parameter pair perform final cell screening.

title: Auxiliary Utils
text: direct R wrapper celltypist.annotate. Unlike SCAnnotate, prepare environment . Parameters: sc: Seurat object. model: Charater/str. model use. NULL, default model used. download: Logical/bool. Whether download model. Defaults TRUE-download models. model already exists, skip download. force_update: Logical. Whether force update model file. conda: Character/str. conda environment name. NULL, try use python. python: Character/str. path python executable. NULL, try use conda. verbose: Logical/bool. Whether print verbose messages. title: Auxiliary Utils
text: Parameters sc : Seurat object pre-computed clusters (stored Idents(sc) sc$seurat_clusters). seurat_obj_markers : Optional pre-computed marker gene table list (output Seurat::FindAllMarkers()). NULL (default), markers computed automatically using parameters passed via .... tissue_name : Character. Biological context annotation (e.g., tissue type, disease state). Helps LLMs interpret marker genes appropriately. Default: "Human Tumor". models : Character vector LLM model identifiers. Supported formats: OpenAI: "gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", etc. Anthropic: "claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620", etc. Google: "gemini-1.5-pro", etc. Alibaba: "qwen-max", "qwen-plus", etc. Default: c("gpt-4o", "claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620", "gemini-1.5-pro", "qwen-max"). single-model mode, first model used. api_keys : Named list API keys provider names keys: openai: OpenAI API key anthropic: Anthropic API key gemini: Google Cloud API key (Gemini enabled) qwen: Alibaba DashScope API key Example: list(openai = "sk-...", anthropic = "sk-ant-..."). Note: Default placeholder keys ("-xxx-key") fail-users must supply valid keys. Returns: Seurat object cell type annotation added metadata columns. helpful link: https://github.com/cafferychen777/mLLMCelltype Privacy data read local input processed official mLLMCelltype — nothing stored servers.
code: seurat <- mLLMCellTypeAnnotate(   sc,   seurat_obj_markers = NULL,   # * Context for large language models   tissue_name = "Human Cancer",   models = c(     "gpt-5",     "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",     "gemini-3-pro",     "qwen-max-2025-01-25"   ),   api_keys = list(     anthropic = "your-anthropic-key",     openai = "your-openai-key",     gemini = "your-google-key",     qwen = "your-qwen-key"   ),   # Other arguments passed to `mLLMCelltype::annotate_cell_types` or ` mLLMCelltype::interactive_consensus_annotation` )

title: Auxiliary Utils
text: Parameters sc: Seurat object. verbose: Logical. Whether print progress messages. Defaults TRUE. ensembl: Logical. Whether convert row names Ensembl IDs. Genes without valid mapping discarded. cell.ont: Character. specifying Cell Ontology term handling. Use "nonna" discard samples without valid terms, "" keep samples (possible NA), "none" skip. legacy: Logical. Whether use legacy ExperimentHub backend. Default uses gypsum. ref: Reference data annotation. Either "HPCA" (Human Primary Cell Atlas celldex) SingleCellExperiment object pre-labeled cells. multiple references, list matrices SummarizedExperiment objects. labels: Character vector cell type labels ref columns. Required custom references; defaults ref$label.main "HPCA". ref list, labels must corresponding list. Returns: Seurat object cell type annotation added metadata columns. helpful link: https://github.com/SingleR-inc/SingleR
code: seurat <- SingleRAnnotate(   sc,   verbose = getFuncOption("verbose"), # TRUE   # * pass to `celldex::HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData`   ensembl = FALSE,   cell.ont = c("all", "nonna", "none"),   legacy = FALSE,   # * pass to `SingleR::SingleR`   ref = c("HPCA", "custom"),   labels = NULL,   # Other arguments passed to `SingleR::SingleR` )

title: Get Started with SigBridgeR
text: start simple example. seurat_obj preprocessed single-cell RNA Seurat object (QC filtering, normalization, clustering, UMAP already included), bulk_bi bulk tissue RNA expression matrix (TPM), pheno_bi phenotypic data associated bulk_bi. using binary continuous phenotype, reference phenotype data named vector. way, using patients’ survival data phenotype, reference data data.frame. reference single-cell RNA data already preprocessed Seurat object (seurat_obj), can passed directly Screen() without processing.
code: ref <- LoadRefData(data_type = "binary") seurat_obj <- ref[[1]] bulk_bi <- ref[[2]] pheno_bi <- ref[[3]] head(pheno_bi) pheno_sur <- LoadRefData(data_type = "survival")[[3]] head(pheno_sur)

title: Get Started with SigBridgeR
text: can use data screen phenotype-assoicated cells. Let’s start trying Scissor. screening methods also available. Since screening performed data, can merge based cell names. Metadata merged well.
code: scissor_res <- Screen(   bulk_bi,   seurat_obj,   pheno_bi,   phenotype_class = "binary",   screen_method = "Scissor",   alpha = 0.05 ) scissor_res |> class() scissor_res |> print() scpas_res <- Screen(   bulk_bi,   seurat_obj,   pheno_bi,   phenotype_class = "binary",   screen_method = "scPAS",   alpha = 0.05 ) merged_seurat <- MergeResult(   scissor_res,   scpas_res )

title: Get Started with SigBridgeR
text: Finally, can visualize screening results. stacked bar plot: Venn diagram: Set plot: 2D UMAP: UMAP registered autoplot() easier check. detail, please see Full Tutorial.
code: fraction <- ScreenFractionPlot(   merged_seurat,   group_by = "seurat_clusters",   screen_type = c("scissor", "scPAS") )  names(fraction)  fraction$combined_plot c(scissor_pos, scpas_pos) %<-%   purrr::map(     c("scissor", "scPAS"),     ~ colnames(merged_seurat)[       which(merged_seurat[[.x]] == "Positive")     ]   )  all_cells <- colnames(seurat_obj)  pos_venn <- list(   scissor = scissor_pos,   scpas = scpas_pos,   all_cells = all_cells )  set.seed(123)  venn_plot <- ggVennDiagram::ggVennDiagram(   x = pos_venn,   # * the labels of each group to be shown on the diagram   category.names = c(     "Scissor",     "scPAS",     "All cells"   ),   # * the colors of each group   set_color = c(     "#a33333ff",     "#37ae00ff",     "#008383ff"   ),   label_geom = c("text") ) +   ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#ffb6b6ff") +   ggplot2::ggtitle("Screening Venn Diagram")  venn_plot upset <- ScreenUpset(   merged_seurat,   screen_type = c("scissor", "scPAS") ) names(upset)  upset$plot library(patchwork)  c(   scissor_umap,   scpas_umap ) %<-%   purrr::map(     c("scissor", "scPAS"),     ~ Seurat::DimPlot(       merged_seurat,       group.by = .x,       pt.size = 0.1,       reduction = "umap",       cols = c(         "Neutral" = "#CECECE",         "Positive" = "#ff3333",         "Negative" = "#386c9b"       )     ) +       ggplot2::ggtitle(.x)   )  set.seed(123) cols <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(   length(unique(merged_seurat$seurat_clusters)),   "Set1" )  cluster_umap <- Seurat::DimPlot(   merged_seurat,   group.by = "seurat_clusters",   pt.size = 0.1,   reduction = "umap",   cols = cols ) +   ggplot2::ggtitle("seurat_clusters")   # * Show umaps <- cluster_umap +   scissor_umap +   scpas_umap +   plot_layout(ncol = 2)  umaps ggplot2::autoplot(merged_seurat, group.by = "scPAS")

code: data_dir <- "GSE274103"  samples <- c(   "GSM8443449_PDAC-p1",   "GSM8443450_PDAC-p2",   "GSM8443451_PDAC-p3",   "GSM8443452_PDAC-p4",   "GSM8443453_PDAC-p5" )  spatial_list <- lapply(samples, function(sample) {   seurat <- Load10X_Spatial(     data.dir = file.path(data_dir, sample),     slice = sample,     assay = "Spatial"   )    seurat <- subset(     seurat,     nCount_Spatial > 0L &       nFeature_Spatial > 0L   )    SCTransform(seurat, assay = "Spatial") })  spatials <- merge(   x = spatial_list[[1]],   y = unlist(spatial_list[-1]),   add.cell.ids = samples,   merge.data = TRUE,   project = "Integrated Spatial Seurat" )  # DefaultAssay(spatials) <- "SCT" VariableFeatures(spatials) <- lapply(spatial_list, function(seurat) {   VariableFeatures(seurat) }) |>   unlist() |>   unique() spatials <- RunPCA(spatials) |>   FindNeighbors(dims = 1:30) |>   FindClusters() |>   RunUMAP(dims = 1:30)  # SeuratObject::SaveSeuratRds(spatials, "seurat.rds")

text: scSurvival: Single-cell expression matrix (log-normalized + HVG-selected) + survival data (optional clinical covariates batch labels) -> Survival-associated cell subpopulations CellPhenoX: Single-cell multi-omics data + bulk-level clinical variables, covariates (optional interaction effect terms) -> interpretable score per cell scPrognosis: scRNA-seq count matrix (imputed MAGIC + filtered low coverage/expression) + bulk RNA-seq expression matrix (matched survival time event status) -> breast cancer prognostic gene signatures Cox PH risk prediction model SCellBOW: source scRNA-seq expression matrix + target scRNA-seq expression matrix + (optional) bulk RNA-seq expression matrix paired survival data -> cell embeddings, cluster assignments, UMAP visualizations, phenotype-algebra-derived risk scores survival probability curves individual cell subpopulations. scPER: Single-cell RNA-seq data + bulk RNA-seq data + celltype annotation (optional batch labels) -> phenotype-associated cell populations

what: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
text: quantitative framework selecting optimal normalization strategies (e.g., SCTransform vs. LogNormalization) based diagnostic metrics rather heuristics. Evaluates three critical dimensions preprocessing quality: Variance stabilization: Decoupling mean-variance relationship normalized expression (lower correlation = better). Biological signal retention: Preservation known marker genes within highly variable genes (higher retention = better). Dropout robustness: Removal technical dropout bias normalized values (lower correlation dropout rate = better). Methods ranked using weighted composite score. Designed head--head comparison preprocessed Seurat objects.

title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
code: ChooseNormalization(   ...,   subset_size = integer(),   known_hvgs = list(),   n_hvgs = 2000L,   low_expressed_thresh = 0.2,   weight = c(variance_stability = 0.4, marker_signal = 0.35, dropout_robustness = 0.25),   verbose = getFuncOption("verbose"),   seed = getFuncOption("seed") )

title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
text: ... Named arguments value Seurat object representing distinct preprocessing strategy (e.g., SCT = sct_obj, Log = log_obj). Requirements: Must named (names become method identifiers) Must contain normalized data data slot specified assay/layer Must identical cell counts (fair comparison) subset_size Integer. Number cells subsample diagnostics. missing empty, defaults min(10000, total_cells). Smaller subsets accelerate computation minimal accuracy loss large datasets (>50k cells). known_hvgs Named list canonical marker genes cell types. Format: list(cell_type1 = c("geneA", "geneB"), cell_type2 = c("geneC", ...)). Used compute marker_retention metric. NULL (default), metric omitted scoring. n_hvgs Integer. Number top highly variable genes evaluate marker retention. Default: 2000L. relevant known_hvgs provided. low_expressed_thresh Numeric (0-1). Quantile threshold filtering lowly expressed genes variance-mean correlation calculation. Genes quantile mean expression excluded. Default: 0.2 (bottom 20% excluded). weight Named numeric vector specifying weights composite scoring. Must contain exactly components summing 1: variance_stability: Weight variance-mean decoupling (default: 0.4) marker_signal: Weight marker gene retention (default: 0.35) dropout_robustness: Weight dropout bias removal (default: 0.25) verbose Logical. Whether print progress messages. seed Integer. Seed reproducible random sampling.

title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
text: list containing: metrics: data.table diagnostic metrics per method: variance_mean_cor: Pearson correlation log10(mean) log10(variance) normalized expression (lower = better) marker_retention: Proportion known markers top HVGs (higher = better; NA known_hvgs provided) mean_dropout_residual: Absolute Spearman correlation dropout rate (counts) normalized means (lower = better) composite_score: Weighted combination normalized metrics (0-1 scale) rank: Method ranking (1 = best) recommendation: Character string naming top-ranked method plots: (Optional) Diagnostic visualizations ggplot2 available

title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
text: Validates input objects (naming, cell count consistency, data slot presence) Subsamples cells (needed) computational efficiency Computes three core metrics per method: Variance stabilization: Correlation log-transformed mean variance normalized expression Marker retention: Overlap user-provided markers top HVGs Dropout robustness: Correlation gene dropout rate (counts) normalized expression means Normalizes metrics 0-1 scale (inverting lower=better) Computes weighted composite score ranks methods Returns top recommendation full diagnostic report

title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
text: Requires pre-normalized Seurat objects-function perform normalization . Users must first run SCTransform(), NormalizeData(), etc., store results data slot. Marker retention metric computed known_hvgs provided. Without , scoring relies solely variance stabilization dropout robustness. Weights sum 1 (enforced recommended interpretable scores).

text: select_fraction top percentage selected cells considered Positive cells, without considering much larger possible correlation coefficient observation group compared control group. usedl phenotype_class "binary" "survival". (default: 0.05) min_thresh DEGAS calculate possible correlation coefficients cell related phenotype. coefficient observation group least min_thresh larger control group, can considered related phenotype marked Positive. priority min_thresh higher select_fraction. (default: 0.4) matched_bulk Bulk RNA-seq data matrix data.frame (rows=genes, columns=samples) sc_data Single-cell data Seurat object containing RNA assay phenotype Bulk-level phenotype data. classification: binary matrix one-hot encoding. survival: matrix two columns (time event status). Can NULL, matrix, data.frame, vector. sc_data.pheno_colname Column name single-cell phenotype metadata (available), default: NULL label_type Label type DEGAS results (default: "DEGAS") phenotype_class Type phenotype: "binary" (classification), "continuous", "survival" tmp_dir (Soft-deprecated) Temporary directory DEGAS intermediate files (default: "DEGAS_res"). Acts fallback load_cache save_cache specified via .... Prefer using load_cache / save_cache ... instead. See CacheSetHere(). env_params List environment parameters Python setup including: env.name: environment name (default: "r-reticulate-degas") env.type: environment type "conda", "environment", "venv" (default: "environment") env.method: environment setup method "system", "conda" (default: "system") env.file: path environment file (default: system.file("conda/DEGAS_environment.yml", package = "SigBridgeR")) env.python_version: Python version (default: "3.9.15") env.packages: named vector Python packages versions (default: c("tensorflow" = "2.4.1", "protobuf" = "3.20" ,"numpy" = "")) env.recreate: whether recreate environment (default: FALSE) env.use_conda_forge: whether use conda-forge channel (conda , default: TRUE) env.verbose: verbose output (default: FALSE) degas_params List DEGAS algorithm parameters including: DEGAS.model_type: model type ("BlankClass", "ClassBlank", "ClassClass", "ClassCox", "BlankCox") DEGAS.architecture: "Standard" (feed forward) "DenseNet" (dense net), default: "DenseNet" DEGAS.ff_depth: number layers model (>=1, default: 3) DEGAS.pyloc: path Python executable (default: NULL, automatic detection) DEGAS.bag_depth: bootstrap aggregation depth (>=1, default: 5) DEGAS.train_steps: training steps (default: 2000) DEGAS.scbatch_sz: single-cell batch size (default: 200) DEGAS.patbatch_sz: patient batch size (default: 50) DEGAS.hidden_feats: hidden features (default: 50) DEGAS.do_prc: dropout percentage (default: 0.5) DEGAS.lambda1: regularization parameter 1 (default: 3.0) DEGAS.lambda2: regularization parameter 2 (default: 3.0) DEGAS.lambda3: regularization parameter 3 (default: 3.0) DEGAS.seed: random seed (default: 2) normality_test_method Method normality testing: "jarque-bera", "d'agostino", "kolmogorov-smirnov" ... Additional arguments. Currently supports: verbose: Logical indicating whether print progress messages. Defaults TRUE. assay: Name assay use. Can : Vector: named sample IDs Data frame: row names matching bulk columns phenotype_class Analysis mode: "binary": Case-control design (e.g., responder/non-responder) "continuous": Continuous outcome (e.g., age, size) "survival": Patient survival only_pos_marker logical value. TRUE, upregulated marker genes (positive log2 fold change) retained. Must sorted ascending order. label_type Character specifying phenotype label type (e.g., "SBS1", "time"), stored scRNA_data@misc marker_finder character, marker finder method. default value "limma". log2FC DESeq differential expression analysis results, cutoff value log2FC. default value 1L. p_adjust DESeq differential expression analysis results, cutoff value adjust P. default value 0.05. show_log2FC Select whether show log2 fold changes. default value TRUE. freq_counts integer, keep genes expressed certain number cells. default value NULL, means filtering. normalize Select whether perform normalization count data. default value TRUE. scale Select whether scale center features dataset. default value TRUE. nPerm integer, number permutations . default value 1000L. distance character, distance algorithm must included "cosine", "pearson", "spearman", "kendall","euclidean","maximum". default value "cosine". ... title: PhenoMapR: Bulk-to-Single-Cell Phenotype Mapping — DoPhenoMapR
text: matched_bulk Matrix data frame bulk expression (genes x samples). Column names must match phenotype names/row names. sc_data Seurat object containing cells scored. phenotype Phenotype data. named vector binary/continuous traits, data frame time--event event columns survival traits; names/row names must match colnames(matched_bulk). label_type Character. meta.data column receiving phenotype group. Default: "PhenoMapR". phenotype_class One "binary", "survival", "continuous". phenotype_column Character. Column name phenotype outcome. phenotype_type = "survival" ignored; use survival_time survival_event instead. survival_time Character. Column name phenotype time--event (e.g. overall survival time). Required phenotype_type = "survival". survival_event Character. Column name phenotype event indicator (0/1 FALSE/TRUE). Required phenotype_type = "survival". normalize Logical. TRUE, run normalization expression looks like counts (default TRUE). Set FALSE skip. platform One "auto", "rnaseq", "microarray". Microarray inputs follow PRECOG preprocessing strategy: optional probe--gene mapping, log2 transform needed, removal zero-variance genes samples/genes heavy missingness, per-study quantile normalization, per-gene unit variance scaling across samples. RNA-seq inputs use log2(CPM+1) matrix looks like raw counts. probe_annotation Optional data.frame probe IDs gene symbols (required probe-level microarray matrices unless row names already gene symbols). See collapse_probes_to_genes. hugo_species Character. Species HUGO symbol cleaning: "human" "mouse" (default "human"). binary_positive_reference phenotype_type "binary" : level binary factor correspond positive outcome logistic regression (y = 1), genes positive z-scores whose higher expression associated level. Use "first" first level factor(..., levels = c(...)) phenotype interest (e.g. mutated vs wt); use "second" legacy convention (second level coded y = 1). Default "second" preserves behaviour previous versions levels implicit (e.g. alphabetical). assay Assay name Seurat/SCE objects (default: "RNA" sc, "Spatial" spatial) layer Seurat matrix score ("data" normalized, "counts" raw, "scale.data"; default "data"). Seurat v5 terminology. PhenoMapR maps GetAssayData(layer=...) GetAssayData(slot=...) based installed SeuratObject version. z_score_cutoff Absolute z-score threshold filtering genes (default: 2). Built-PRECOG/TCGA matrices shipped package already sparse cutoff (entries \(|z| \leq 2\) stored NA; see precog, tcga), lowering cutoff 2 recover discarded associations unless denser custom reference supplied. reference_sign Multiply reference gene z-scores value weighted sum. Use 1 (default) -1 flip sign resulting PhenoMap scores without changing reference matrix (e.g. want positive scores mean opposite association). custom references derive_reference_from_bulk, prefer setting binary_positive_reference reference matches factor levels (first level = positive association "first"). score_mode Scoring mode: "weighted_sum" (default) uses standard dot product expression reference z-scores; "activity_adjusted" regresses technical covariates per gene (via Seurat ScaleData) computing weighted sum regressed layer. Requires Seurat matrix inputs. vars_to_regress Metadata columns regress score_mode = "activity_adjusted". Default: c("S.Score", "G2M.Score", "nCount_RNA"). matrix input, pass covariates via sample_metadata (see ). nCount_RNA computed column sums absent. cancer_type Cancer type label. Required using built-reference datasets. match column names reference data. ICI PRECOG, use format "ABBREV" "ABBREV_Metastatic" (e.g., "MELANOMA", "MELANOMA_Metastatic") pseudobulk Logical. TRUE, aggregate expression scoring (default: FALSE) group_by Column name pseudobulk grouping. Required pseudobulk = TRUE. Seurat/SCE objects, metadata column. sample_metadata Optional data.frame per-cell/sample covariates score_mode = "activity_adjusted" expression matrix. Must include cell identifier column (default "cell_id"). percentile Fraction cells tail (default 0.05 top bottom 5%). permutation_n positive integer, compute gene-shuffle permutation null scores add empirical_p_* columns alongside raw score columns. permutation_seed Random seed permutation null (default 42). ... Additional arguments reserved method compatibility. seed Integer. Random seed. Default: getFuncOption("seed"). verbose Logical. Whether print progress messages. Default: getFuncOption("verbose").

title: PhenoMapR: Bulk-to-Single-Cell Phenotype Mapping — DoPhenoMapR
text: define_phenotype_groups() labels upper tail score distribution "Adverse" lower tail "Favorable". score increases towards phenotype-valued--1 end reference derived default orientation (numeric 0/1 phenotype, binary_positive_reference = "second" regresses "1" level, survival traits Cox z-score positive hazard-increasing genes). Therefore, phenotype 1 denotes unfavourable direction, "Adverse" tail one labelled "Positive"; group labels mapped package-wide vocabulary "Adverse" -> "Positive", "Favorable" -> "Negative" "" -> "Neutral". Setting reference_sign = -1 mirrors score axis, case two tails swap. phenotype encoded adverse class reference-positive level (e.g. binary_positive_reference = "first" numeric 0/1 labels), score direction reversed well; choose arguments higher scores track adverse phenotype.

title: Screen Single-Cell Data Using SCIPAC Algorithm — DoSCIPAC
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Example 1: Binary phenotype (case/control) library(SCIPAC)  # Prepare data bulk_expr <- matrix(rpois(1000, 10), nrow = 200, ncol = 5) colnames(bulk_expr) <- paste0("Sample", 1:5) rownames(bulk_expr) <- paste0("Gene", 1:200)  seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = matrix(rpois(2000, 5), nrow = 200, ncol = 10))  phenotype_binary <- c(Sample1 = 1, Sample2 = 0, Sample3 = 1, Sample4 = 0, Sample5 = 1)  # Run SCIPAC screening result <- DoSCIPAC(   matched_bulk = bulk_expr,   sc_data = seurat_obj,   phenotype = phenotype_binary,   phenotype_class = "binary",   hvg = 100,   resolution = 1,   verbose = TRUE )  # Access results screened_seurat <- result$scRNA_data head(screened_seurat[[]])  # Example 2: Survival analysis survival_data <- data.frame(   time = c(12.5, 24.3, 18.7, 36.2, 30.1),   status = c(1, 0, 1, 1, 0),   row.names = paste0("Sample", 1:5) )  result <- DoSCIPAC(   matched_bulk = bulk_expr,   sc_data = seurat_obj,   phenotype = survival_data,   phenotype_class = "survival",   ela_net_alpha = 0.5,   bt_size = 100,   ncore = 4 )  # Example 3: Continuous phenotype with custom parameters continuous_pheno <- c(Sample1 = 25.3, Sample2 = 45.7, Sample3 = 38.2,                       Sample4 = 52.1, Sample5 = 31.8)  result <- DoSCIPAC(   matched_bulk = bulk_expr,   sc_data = seurat_obj,   phenotype = continuous_pheno,   phenotype_class = "continuous",   hvg = 500,   n_pc = 30,   resolution = 2,   ela_net_alpha = 0.3,   ci_alpha = 0.01,   seed = 42 )  # View screening parameters used result$scRNA_data@misc$SCIPAC_params  # Example 4: With batch correction seurat_obj$batch_id <- sample(c("Batch1", "Batch2"), ncol(seurat_obj), replace = TRUE)  result <- DoSCIPAC(   matched_bulk = bulk_expr,   sc_data = seurat_obj,   phenotype = phenotype_binary,   phenotype_class = "binary",   sc_batch_col = "batch_id",   ncore = 8 ) } # }

title: Perform TiRank Screening Analysis — DoTiRank
text: TiRank screening workflow consists following steps: Data preprocessing: Normalizes bulk expression data validates compatibility phenotype information. Expression transfer: Transfers single-cell expression profile TiRank-compatible format. Validation set generation: Splits bulk data training validation sets according validation_proportion. Resampling: Applies specified sampling strategy address class imbalance bulk data. Cell-cell similarity: Computes cell-cell distance similarity matrix single-cell data. Model training: Trains TiRank neural network (MLP, Transformer, DenseNet encoder) using bulk expression phenotype. Screening: Applies trained model score cell, producing rank-based predictions rejection handling. Label assignment: Classifies cells "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative" based rank scores.

code: # A typical bulk RNA-seq raw counts matrix (genes x samples) counts <- matrix(   c(100, 200, 300, 150, 250, 350),   nrow = 3, ncol = 2,   dimnames = list(c("GENE1", "GENE2", "GENE3"), c("Sample1", "Sample2")) ) IsCountsMatrix(counts) #> ✔ Result: TRUE; matrix is likely a counts matrix (integer fraction among non-zero 1.000000, density 1.000000) #> [1] TRUE  # A log-normalized matrix is not counts IsCountsMatrix(log1p(counts)) #> ℹ Result: FALSE; insufficient integer-like values among non-zero entries (integer fraction 0.000000 < threshold 0.950000) #> [1] FALSE  # Matrices containing negative values are not counts IsCountsMatrix(counts - 1000) #> ℹ Result: FALSE; matrix contains negative values #> [1] FALSE  # Inspect diagnostic statistics IsCountsMatrix(counts, verbose = TRUE) #> ✔ Result: TRUE; matrix is likely a counts matrix (integer fraction among non-zero 1.000000, density 1.000000) #> [1] TRUE

what: Test Whether the Proportion of a Target Value Is Highly Skewed — IsSkewedDynamic
title: Test Whether the Proportion of a Target Value Is Highly Skewed — IsSkewedDynamic
text: IsSkewedDynamic() tests whether observed proportion specified target/background value vector deviates substantially expected proportion. function designed detecting highly skewed phenotype-like vectors, especially binary discrete vectors one value represents background/control class. observed proportion target differs expected_p n_sd standard deviations binomial model, vector considered skewed. Formally, let: $$\hat{p} = \frac{\#(x_i = target)}{n}$$ $$SD = \sqrt{\frac{expected\_p(1 - expected\_p)}{n}}$$ function returns TRUE : $$|\hat{p} - expected\_p| > n\_sd \times SD$$ Otherwise, returns FALSE. x length zero, function returns NA.

title: Single-Cell RNA-seq Preprocessing Pipeline — SCPreProcess
text: sc Input data. Can : Matrix/Data frame: Raw count matrix (genes x cells). AnnData: Python AnnData object (read via anndata anndataR packages). Seurat: Seurat object (automatically validated repaired necessary). ... Additional arguments backward compatibility (mapped params) verbose control. pipeline character string defining processing steps order. Characters map Seurat functions: 'o': CreateSeuratObject (Must first step deleted) 'n': NormalizeData 's': ScaleData 'v': FindVariableFeatures 'p': RunPCA 'e': FindNeighbors ("n" used) 'c': FindClusters 't': RunTSNE 'u': RunUMAP 'r': SCTransform (Alternative n/s/v) Default "onsvpcetu". params named list lists containing arguments pipeline step. Keys match pipeline characters (e.g., params$n NormalizeData). Default structure: quality_control list containing regex patterns QC metric calculation. (See QCPatternDetect) Default: list(pattern = "^MT-"). Detected metrics (e.g., percent.mt) added meta.data. data_filter list thresholds cell filtering. Default: assay ("RNA"), nFeature_RNA (200-6000), nCount_RNA (500-50000), percent.mt (<20), percent.rp (<60). metrics detected via quality_control filtered, .e., nFeature_RNA, nCount_RNA percent.mt. column2only_tumor Optional character. Column name metadata filter tumor cells (matches "Tumor", "Cancer", "Malignant", etc.). NULL, filtering performed.

Column names must match names/IDs phenotype. sc_data Seurat object containing scRNA-seq data screened. phenotype Phenotype data, either: Named vector, names match columns matched_bulk Patient survival data frame, row names match columns matched_bulk, column names "time" "status" label_type Character specifying phenotype label type, e.g. "SBS1" "time". phenotype_class Type phenotypic outcome. Must consistent input data: "binary": Binary traits, e.g. case/control "continuous": Continuous measurements "survival": Survival information screen_method Screening algorithm use. Available options: "DEGASv2": see also DoDEGASv2() "Scissor": see also DoScissor() "TiRank": see also DoTiRank() "SCIPAC": see also DoSCIPAC() "scPP": see also DoscPP() "LP_SGL": see also DoLP_SGL() "PIPET": see also DoPIPET() "DEGAS": see also DoDEGAS() "scAB": see also DoscAB() "PhenoMapR": see also DoPhenoMapR() "SIDISH": see also DoSIDISH() "scPAS": see also DoscPAS() ... Additional method-specific parameters. Scissor alpha: Numeric NULL. Significance threshold. NULL, alpha increases iteratively corresponding cells screened . Default: 0.05. cutoff: Numeric. Threshold terminating iteration alpha; works alpha = NULL. Default: 0.2. path2load_scissor_cache: Character. Default: NULL. path2save_scissor_inputs: Character. Path save intermediary data. Can loaded later via path2load_scissor_cache. Default: "Scissor_inputs.RData". reliability_test: Logical. Whether perform reliability test. Default: FALSE. reliability_test.nfold: Integer. Cross-validation folds reliability test. Default: 10. reliability_test.n: Integer. Number cells use reliability test. Default: 10. cell_evaluation: Logical. Whether perform cell evaluation. Default: FALSE. cell_evaluation.benchmark_data: .RData benchmark data cell evaluation. Default: NULL. cell_evaluation.FDR: Numeric. FDR threshold cell evaluation. Default: 0.05. cell_evaluation.bootstrap_n: Integer. Number bootstrap samples cell evaluation. Default: 10. scPP ref_group: Integer character. Reference group baseline binary comparisons, e.g. "Normal" 0. Default: 0. Log2FC_cutoff: Numeric. Minimum log2 fold-change binary markers. Default: 0.585. estimate_cutoff: Numeric. Effect size threshold continuous traits. Default: 0.2. probs: Numeric. Quantile cutoff cell classification. Default: 0.2. scPAS assay: Character. Assay use sc_data. Default: "RNA". imputation: Logical. Whether perform imputation. Default: FALSE. nfeature: Integer. Number features select. Default: 3000. alpha: Numeric NULL. Significance threshold. NULL, alpha increases iteratively corresponding cells screened . Default: 0.01. independent: Logical. Whether background distribution risk scores constructed independently cell. Default: TRUE. network_class: Character. Network class use. Default: "SC" single-cell-derived gene-gene similarity networks; another option "bulk". permutation_times: Integer. Number permutations. Default: 2000. FDR_threshold: Numeric. FDR threshold identifying phenotype-associated cells. Default: 0.05. scAB alpha: Numeric. Coefficient phenotype regularization. Default: 0.005. alpha_2: Numeric. Coefficient cell-cell similarity regularization. Default: 0.005. maxiter: Integer. NMF optimization iterations. Default: 2000. tred: Integer. Z-score threshold. Default: 2. DEGAS sc_data.pheno_colname: Character. Phenotype column name sc_data. Default: "NULL". select_fraction: Numeric. Fraction cells select DEGAS. Default: 0.05. tmp_dir: Character. Temporary directory DEGAS. Default: "NULL". env_params: List. Environment parameters DEGAS. Default: list(). degas_params: List. DEGAS parameters. Default: list(). normality_test_method: Character. Normality test method DEGAS. Default: "jarque-bera". SIDISH sidish_params: List. SIDISH parameters. Default: list(). env_params: List. Environment parameters SIDISH. Default: list(). SCIPAC hvg: Integer. Number highly variable genes use preprocessing. Default: 1000. do_pca_sc: Logical. TRUE, first PCA sc.dat use rotation matrix bulk.dat; FALSE, first PCA bulk.data use rotation matrix sc.dat. Default: FALSE. n_pc: Integer. Number principal components use. Default: 60. sc_batch_col: Character vector. Batch variable single-cell data. character, column name sc_data@metadata. vector, match cell order. Default: NULL. resolution: Integer. Clustering resolution cell type identification. Higher values produce clusters. Default: 2. ela_net_alpha: Numeric. Elastic net mixing parameter (0 = ridge, 1 = lasso). Default: 0.4. bt_size: Integer. Bootstrap sample size stability assessment. Default: 50. ncore: Integer. Number CPU cores parallel computation. Default: 7. ci_alpha: Numeric. Significance level confidence intervals. Default: 0.05. nfold: Integer. Number folds cross-validation. Default: 10. assay: Character. Assay use sc_data. Default: "RNA". verbose: Logical. Whether print progress messages. Default: inherits getFuncOption("verbose"). seed: Integer. Random seed reproducibility. Default: 123. PIPET group: Character NULL. Metadata column used stratify cells screening. Default: NULL. discretize_method: Character. Strategy binarize continuous phenotypes: "median": Median threshold. Default. "kmeans": Two-cluster k-means. "custom": User-defined cutoffs via cutoff. cutoff: Numeric vector NULL. Required discretize_method = "custom". Specifies interior breakpoints normalized, log2-transformed phenotype scale, scale(log2(x + 1)). label_type: Character. Phenotype label type stored scRNA_data@misc. Default: "PIPET". log2FC: Numeric. Absolute log2 fold-change cutoff bulk marker selection. Default: 1. p_adjust: Numeric. Adjusted p-value/FDR cutoff marker selection. Default: 0.05. show_log2FC: Logical. Whether annotate markers signed log2FC direction. Default: TRUE. freq_counts: Integer NULL. Minimum number cells gene must expressed . Default: NULL. normalize: Logical. Whether apply LogNormalize correlation. Default: TRUE. scale: Logical. Whether center scale gene expression computing distances. Default: TRUE. nPerm: Integer. Number label permutations. Default: 1000. distance: Character. Supported metrics: "cosine", "pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "euclidean", "maximum". Default: "cosine". seed: Integer NULL. Random seed. Default: inherits getFuncOption("seed"). verbose: Logical. Whether print progress messages. Default: inherits getFuncOption("verbose"). parallel: Logical. Whether enable parallel permutations. Requires future::plan() pre-set. Default: FALSE. LP_SGL resolution: Numeric. Resolution parameter Leiden clustering. Default: 0.6. alpha: Numeric. SGL parameter balancing L1 L2 penalties. Default: 0.5. nfold: Integer. Number folds cross-validation. Default: 5. dge_analysis: List. Differential expression analysis settings: run: Logical. Whether run DEG analysis. Default: FALSE. logFC_threshold: Numeric. Log fold-change threshold. Default: 1. pval_threshold: Numeric. P-value threshold. Default: 0.05. DEGASv2 top_fraction_pos: Numeric. Proportion cells labelled "Positive". Default: 0.2. sclab: Character NULL. Metadata column providing supervised cell labels. Default: NULL. bulk_hvg: Logical. Whether select highly variable genes bulk data. Default: TRUE. bulk_de: Logical. Whether perform differential expression analysis bulk data. Default: TRUE. sc_de: Logical. Whether perform differential expression analysis single-cell data. Default: TRUE. add_genes: Character vector NULL. Additional genes include analysis. Default: NULL. n_hvg: Integer. Number highly variable genes select. Default: 250. n_bulk_de: Integer. Number bulk DE genes select. Default: 250. n_sc_de: Integer. Number single-cell DE genes select. Default: 200. padj.thresh: Numeric. Adjusted p-value threshold DE gene selection. Default: 0.05. .pos: Logical. Whether keep positively enriched markers. Default: FALSE. min.pct: Numeric. Minimum fraction cells expressing gene DE analysis. Default: 0.25. logfc.threshold: Numeric. Log fold-change threshold DE analysis. Default: 0.25. n_st_classes: Integer. Number single-cell classes. Default: length(unique(sc_data$seurat_clusters)). loss_type: Character. Loss function model training. One "cross_entropy", "log_neg", "rank_loss". Default: "cross_entropy". transfer_type: Character. Weight classification loss. Default: 1. lambda2: Numeric. Weight domain-adaptation loss. Default: 3. lambda3: Numeric. Weight reconstruction loss. Default: 3. tot_seeds: Integer. Number random seeds train. Default: 10. tot_iters: Integer. Number training iterations. Default: 300. extract_embs: Logical. Whether extract cell embeddings. Default: FALSE. random_feat: Logical. Whether use random features. Default: FALSE. random_perc: Numeric. Proportion random features random_feat = TRUE. Default: 0.8. early_stopping: Logical. Whether enable early stopping. Default: FALSE. TiRank tirank_params: List. See DoTiRank() details. Default: list(). save_path: Character. Directory save intermediate final results. Soft-deprecated; prefer passing load_cache/save_cache via ... Default: "./TiRank_res". load_cache: Character NULL. Path cached TiRank data. Soft-deprecated; prefer passing load_cache via ... Default: NULL. verbose: Logical. Whether print progress messages. Default: inherits getFuncOption("verbose"). seed: Integer. Random seed reproducibility. Default: inherits getFuncOption("seed"). assay: Character. Assay use sc_data. text: Performs automated cell type annotation Seurat clusters leveraging multiple large language models (LLMs) interpret cluster-specific marker genes. function supports single-model annotation multi-model consensus generation, uncertainty quantification via agreement metrics. Supported formats: OpenAI: "gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", etc. Anthropic: "claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620", etc. Google: "gemini-1.5-pro", etc. Alibaba: "qwen-max", "qwen-plus", etc. single-model mode (length(models) == 1), first model used via mLLMCelltype::annotate_cell_types(). Must provided. Default: character(). api_keys Named vector API keys provider names keys: openai: OpenAI API key anthropic: Anthropic API key gemini: Google Cloud API key (Gemini enabled) qwen: Alibaba DashScope API key Example: list(openai = "sk-...", anthropic = "sk-ant-..."). Must provided named; placeholder keys (e.g., "-xxx-key") fail. Default: list(). top_gene_count Integer. Number top marker genes per cluster passed LLMs. Default: 10. debug Logical. Maximum number discussion rounds consensus process. Default: 3. consensus_check_model Character. Model used check consensus discussion. Default: NULL (use first model). log_dir Character. Directory saving consensus process logs. Default: "logs". cache_dir Character. Directory caching API responses. Default: NULL. use_cache Logical. Whether use cached API responses. Default: TRUE. clusters_to_analyze Character integer vector. Subset cluster IDs analyze; NULL analyzes clusters. Default: NULL. force_rerun Logical. Whether ignore cached results re-run annotation. title: SigBridgeR 4.0.0
text: Added GetGeneLength() FPKMToTPM() extracting gene lengths GTF annotations converting FPKM TPM. GetGeneLength() supports canonical_chr_only option preserves gene ID versions. Added DoPhenoMapR() screening method PhenoMapR, mapping bulk phenotypes single-cell subpopulations, ValidatePhenoMapRParams() input alignment parameter checks. registered ScreenStrategy available Screen(). Introduced benchmarking framework: BenchAcc(), BenchGSEA(), BenchGeneScore() BenchMemory(), along S7 configuration classes (BenchConfig, BenchAccConfig, BenchGSEAConfig, BenchGeneScoreConfig, BenchMemoryConfig, MethodParamSet *ConfigSet helpers). BenchAcc() now also reports Precision Recall. Exported AVAILABLE_SCREEN_METHODS AVAILABLE_ANNOTATE_METHODS; ScreenStrategy registry replaces ad-hoc names(ScreenStrategy) lookups. SymbolConvert() now accepts character vectors, offers update_symbol_method ("scCustomize", "Seurat" "auto"), supports extended genome builds, replaces unmatched/duplicated symbols original IDs; unknown_format deprecated ignored. Added + operator merging ScreenMethodResult objects S3 methods merging Seurat objects. autoplot() interactively prompts group.multiple candidates available. Added list_to_chr_formated(), renders list indented multi-line string; list_to_chr() print() method SigBridgeRBase objects now backed C++. SetThreads() (renamed setThreads()) gains Seurat thread-config backend; WGCNA backend renamed wgcna.

title: SigBridgeR 4.0.0
text: FindRobustElbow() offloads elbow detection C++ using tatami streaming caps ndims number available PCs. FPKMToTPM() / GetGeneLength() stream GTF files zlib buffered reader single-pass C++ validation. Replaced utils::modifyList() custom C++ modify_list() added nthreads option. BenchMemory() serialises staged inputs compress_level = 1 derives qs2 thread count ; uses least two cores skips machine-resource probe probe_resources = FALSE. Matrix handling now uses beachmat.

title: SigBridgeR 4.0.0
text: Minimum requirements raised: R >= 4.2.0, S7 >= 1.0.0, C++17 zlib (>= 1.2.4) (previously R >= 4.1.0, S7 >= 1.0.0, C++14). CacheSysCall() load mode now requires explicit path. SymbolConvert()’s unknown_format argument deprecated ignored. PIPET_Screen() now defaults distance "cosine"; DoDEGAS() defaults normality_test_method "jarque-bera". setThreads() renamed SetThreads(); WGCNA backend renamed wgcna. WGCNA backend now requires least two threads: values 2L raised 2L (warning verbose = TRUE).
